title: Deployment constraint mapping and rolling playbook for enterprise POC
content:
Purpose:
Quick rolling playbook + constraint map for Customer X POC. Goal: reduce surprises during deployment week, give on-call / SEs a clear escalation ladder, and a lightweight task tracker for the two-week technical engagement.

Background:
Customer X wants a private/in-region POC that demonstrates realtime chat (<=250ms median per token) and document embeddings for search. They require KMS integration, audit logs, and data residency. Budgeted for 2-week hands-on POC with follow-on production discussion.

High-level scope (what we will demo):
- Hosted/private hybrid: control plane in Redwood cloud, inference nodes in customer VPC (BYO NICs)
- Chat model (redwood-llama-7b-q4) + embeddings (open-embed-768)
- Canary: start with low-QPS single GPU, scale to 4x on dedicated nodes
- End-to-end: demo API + Console observability + cost-per-request dashboard

Success criteria (customer & internal):
- Customer: 90% of demo queries completed with end-to-end latency <= 400ms (including network).
- Internal: KMS integration verified for 100% of persisted checkpoints; audit logs flowing to their SIEM for 48 hours.
- Business: Customer commits to next-phase evaluation if 3 functional flows pass acceptance tests.

Constraint mapping (quick reference):
- Network: customer firewall blocks outbound to S3 except specific prefixes. Action: list required endpoints and open with infra team (ticket JIRA-POC-987).
- KMS: AES-256 keys only; HSM not required. Action: schedule KMS handshake on Day 0, crypto team on call.
- Bandwidth: customer VPC reports 400 Mbps egress cap during POC windows. Estimate token traffic for burst at 1k qps -> likely throttle. Plan for batching and token caps.
- Latency budget: customer wants 400ms E2E. With 1x A10G and model config we estimate 120–180ms server-side for 512-token context with quantized model. Must measure network hops.
- Compliance: no persisted PII on our managed storage. Use ephemeral PVCs and scrub logs before retention.

Rolling playbook (canary -> ramp -> steady):
1) Canary (Day 1 morning): one GPU node, route 1% traffic, strict telemetry, enable detailed tracing. Duration: 4 hours.
2) Observe & validate (Day 1 afternoon): run acceptance set (prompt suite) with perf and quality checks. If pass -> proceed.
3) Stage ramp (Day 2): scale to 2 nodes, route 10% traffic, enable autoscaling buffer. Monitor latency P50/P95 and token cost.
4) Full ramp (Day 3): scale to target 4 nodes, route 100% demo traffic. Keep fallback to small model variant and region fallback policy active.
5) Fallback / degrade path: if P95 > SLA for 5 minutes -> auto-failover to cheaper variant OR reduce max_context to 256 tokens and signal client.

Week-by-week timeline (two-week engagement):
Week 0 (prep):
- Deliverables: network whitelist, KMS access, sample data drop, acceptance prompts.
- Owners: Owen (network), Priya (KMS), Marco (data ingestion).

Week 1 (setup & canary):
Mon: infra provisioning, kube nodes in customer VPC, attach CSI driver.
Tue: deploy inference runtime, load model artifacts (ephemeral).
Wed: canary traffic + validation tests.
Thu: run workshop w/ customer devs on integration (sample code walkthru).
Fri: collect telemetry, cost estimates, short retro.

Week 2 (ramp & handoff):
Mon: scale & resilience tests (inject latency, simulate GPU OOM).
Tue: integration QA, embedding ingestion for search demo.
Wed: SRE handover, runbook walkthrough.
Thu: exec demo + acceptance gate.
Fri: capture artifacts, deliver follow-up proposal.

Task tracker (mini):
- Network whitelist provided by customer — Owner: Owen Liu — Status: in_progress — ETA: 2025-07-10
- KMS key created & access policy validated — Owner: Priya Nair — Status: scheduled — ETA: 2025-07-09
- Model artifact transfer checklist complete — Owner: Marco Diaz — Status: done — ETA: 2025-07-07
- Acceptance prompt suite uploaded to repo — Owner: Ethan Brooks — Status: in_progress — ETA: 2025-07-11
- Observability dashboard template configured — Owner: Samira Patel — Status: scheduled — ETA: 2025-07-09

Risk register (top 6):
- Risk: Network egress limits cause throttling. Mitigation: precompute embedding batches; request dedicated window for high QPS. Owner: Owen.
- Risk: KMS handshake delays due to corporate approvals. Mitigation: escrow plan using temporary test key. Owner: Priya.
- Risk: Model accuracy regression after quantization. Mitigation: include reference prompts and automated quality tests; fallback to larger FP16 variant. Owner: Marco.
- Risk: Audit logs not ingestable into customer's SIEM. Mitigation: sample log export, map fields, coordinate with their security engineer. Owner: Samira.
- Risk: Unexpected GPU OOM during stress tests. Mitigation: set aggressive batching limits and per-instance token caps. Owner: Ethan.
- Risk: Scheduling overlap with infra team. Mitigation: confirm block times and on-call list. Owner: Ava.

Workshop notes (raw, unedited):
- Customer devs prefer REST over gRPC for now; ask if we should ship a light REST shim.
- They have internal SSO via Okta, want to test SAML SSO for dashboard.
- Asked for cost estimate per 10k queries for both chat and embeddings (include both token and infra amortization).
- Requested sample rollback plan for data retention policy (how we delete temporary artifacts).
- TODO: push small sample repo that uses their PKCS11 HSM (Marco + Priya).

Open questions / decisions needed (notes to self):
- Do we provision ephemeral S3 in their VPC or use pre-signed uploads to our storage? (Impact: audit surface)
- Agree on SLA numbers in writing before ramping beyond canary. (Need legal sign-off?)
- Confirm whether embedding vectors must be encrypted at rest with customer-managed key.

Immediate next steps (for SE squad):
- Send network whitelist template to customer (Owen) — today
- Lock Day 1 morning timeslot for canary (Ava) — today
- Draft one-page acceptance criteria to share in kickoff (Ethan) — EOD
- Create Confluence summary with links to runbooks and playbooks (Marco) — next business day

Appendix: quick capacity estimate (back-of-envelope):
- Model: redwood-llama-7b-q4 -> ~6.5 GB VRAM quantized
- Single A10G style node: ~1.8x throughput baseline @512 context; estimate 80 RPS for chat (1 call per request) at p50 ~140ms token server-side.
- For embedding ingestion: a 4-GPU pool can handle ~1200 embed/sec with batching.
- Cost note: highlight that batching aggressively reduces unit token cost but increases tail latency; pick conservative batch windows for demo.

Notes to release with doc: export acceptance prompt set to repo and link in Confluence, cc: solutions-eng mailing list.
